## 1. Purpose, roles and prerequisites

Apply the concern process using the form and register. Required before actual use: scope, intake/assessment/decision roles, authority limits, escalation contacts, evidence access, agreed risk method and private record location. No physical troubleshooting is prescribed.

## 2. Sequence and controls

1. Reporter records facts and separates inference from observation. Intake owner assigns ID, acknowledges receipt and routes urgency using authorized arrangements.
2. Assessor identifies objective, risk, existing controls and missing information; consults affected roles and records disagreements.
3. Assessor proposes a discrete control with 5W+1H and evidence, implementation actions and a testable outcome criterion. Identify any technical or obligation question requiring a competent determination.
4. Decision authority reviews evidence and remit, records accept/revise/hold with reasons, resources, owners and due triggers. Add to the leadership meeting where the adopted escalation criterion requires it; record agenda reference and decision separately.
5. Receiving owners acknowledge the assigned scope. Missing acknowledgment is an unresolved handoff, not completed acceptance.
6. Action owner performs authorized actions and records implementation. A changed scope returns to assessment/authorization; old evidence is not automatically reusable.
7. Reviewer checks outcome evidence against the agreed criterion using the linked instruction. Missing or adverse evidence retains an open item and triggers revised action or assessment.
8. Delegated authority decides closure only within reviewed scope. Custodian preserves the trail; affected people receive the current decision and any remaining open matters.

## 3. Acceptance, holds and escalation

Accept an intake only when owner/scope/next action are clear; do not refuse urgent reporting because detail is incomplete. Hold treatment/release/closure decisions that depend on missing authority or evidence. Record who resolves the gap and the actual review trigger. A meeting discussion, signature or completed checklist is not evidence of effectiveness by itself.

## 4. Outputs and retained records

Retain original form, assessment, agenda/minute references, decision, acknowledgments, implementation and outcome evidence, closure rationale and corrections. Adopt actual privacy/access/retention rules before real records are collected. This template is not an organizational authorization.

## 5. History

r01: original learning procedure supporting ORR-REQ-GEN-001–008; technical obligations remain configured prerequisites.
